issue.title: Http Gzip Compression
issue.body:
Investigate why Quarkus compression is not working.

```properties
quarkus.http.enable-compression=true
```

body:
@mkouba looks like https://github.com/stuartwdouglas/quarkus/commit/670a205d3870a517001a53006d46ac08c5cb5437 broke compression for Servlet (and likely Resteasy Classic)? 

There is now always a `Content-Encoding: identity` header, which needs to be removed to enable compression. The docs for https://github.com/stuartwdouglas/quarkus/blob/933a7ef7b7b1ec9c6071cf0e52eeae7edd7d1ca4/extensions/vertx-http/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/vertx/http/runtime/HttpBuildTimeConfig.java#L72 are also no longer correct.

Hm, for RESTEasy Classic it's [documented that `quarkus.http.enable-compression` has no effect](https://quarkus.io/guides/resteasy#gzip-support) and `quarkus.resteasy.gzip.enabled=true` plus the `@org.jboss.resteasy.annotations.GZIP` should be used.

The case for servlets was actually never discussed in the scope of https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/24558 and related issues :thinking:. 

I think that we should honor the `quarkus.http.compress-media-types` by default.

@stuartwdouglas I was trying to fix the problem in https://github.com/mkouba/quarkus/commit/e3aceb96c2b004e1a72d0e4775023e44c409c9c0, i.e. wrap the UT handler and remove the `Content-Encoding: identity` header in an "end" handler regitered via `RoutingContext.addEndHandler()`. But the end handler does not seem to be called at all for UT. Do you have an idea about what could be wrong?

Hm, maybe it's because the `VertxHttpExchange` [does set its own end handler](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-http/blob/main/vertx/src/main/java/io/undertow/vertx/VertxHttpExchange.java#L210-L220); so the end handlers added previously are just ignored...

issue.title: HTTP response compression - fix Undertow and RESTEasy Classsic support
issue.body:
- honor the quarkus.http.compress-media-types in Undertow Servlet and RESTEasy Classsic extensions
- fixes #31415 and #26112

body:
> Hm, maybe it's because the `VertxHttpExchange` [does set its own end handler](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-http/blob/main/vertx/src/main/java/io/undertow/vertx/VertxHttpExchange.java#L210-L220); so the end handlers added previously are just ignored...

That seemed to be the cause - a workaround is to add the handler logic after the `VertxHttpExchange` is created.
Thanks you for investigating and resolving @mkouba !
Confirmed this works in my Servlet app in 3.0.0.Alpha5!
